top_choice_rationale: P001 credits one identifiable idea (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice) and one identifiable realisation (Ye's 1e-18 strontium clocks), reproduced in Sr and Yb in several national laboratories and already used for geodesy, constant-drift bounds and the case for redefining the second. Its two-name allocation can be defended name by name, unlike the Higgs trios, and the citation is scoped to the lattice scheme so it stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The Higgs discovery is the larger event, so I rank P002 (Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee: ATLAS and CMS leadership through construction and first running) above P003, which omits Virdee for Della Negra and is less well supported on the discovery-era record. A prize is better than no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: Possible professional connection to the field of P001: long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and Lund and ETH Zurich attosecond groups, and I have supplied atomic-structure calculations for precision and storage-ring work, though none with Katori or Ye is documented in my profile. No connection to the Higgs laureates is apparent from the profile.
